ONLY THESE TWO PEOPLE in the frame. THE QUEEN AND THE MINISTER WHO WANTS HER THRONE. Queen Sunduk, older, crowned, sits on her throne facing the camera, composed, eyes forward, a faint knowing smile. Bidam stands at her shoulder, CLEAN-SHAVEN, in his white robe with galloping horses on the sleeves, leaning down to murmur in her ear, prayer beads in his fingers, smiling, eyes cold and ambitious. She knows; he knows she knows. Warm lamp on her, navy shadow on him. CHARACTER SHEET (copy these faces, hair and clothes exactly): LEFT of the sheet = QUEEN SUNDUK; RIGHT of the sheet = BIDAM. QUEEN SUNDUK — Look: Pale oval face, dark calm eyes; black hair in a full coiled updo; when crowned, the gold Silla tree-and-antler crown hung with jade gogok. Dress: Crimson court robe with gold phoenix brocade, blue embroidered cape-collar, a red ribbon bow at the chest. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. Colour #E8552B. | BIDAM — Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: Long white outer robe whose sleeves are embroidered with galloping horses, over a plum-magenta inner robe and white sash. Navy #141C2E lives in the room and on the beads, not on his clothes. Now: Older Sangdaedeung (stage portrait): grey at the temples, same smile. Colour #141C2E.
